safety: Charge only with a charger made for lithium-ion cells, using constant current then constant voltage (CC/CV) up to the charge voltage in the cell datasheet (4.2 V for cobalt, nickel and manganese chemistries, 3.65 V for lithium iron phosphate).
Do not discharge below the datasheet cutoff voltage (2.5 V for most cells listed here); deep discharge damages the cell and a damaged cell should be discarded.
The metal can is the negative terminal. A torn or missing wrap exposes the can and can short the cell against a metal object or an adjacent cell.

Unprotected cells have no overcharge, over-discharge or short-circuit protection of their own and need protection in the charger or the device; protected cells carry a circuit board but should still be charged with a matching charger.

Transport limits apply: the U.S. FAA requires spare lithium-ion cells to travel in carry-on baggage with the terminals protected against short circuit, and limits rechargeable lithium-ion batteries to 100 Wh each (FAA PackSafe).
